transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-18 | Start: 16:32 UTC | Duration: 56m
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Nguyen (Redwood SE), Anika Bose (Cypherware Head of ML), Marcus Liu (Infra Lead), Priya Shah (Product PM)
Recording: Yes
Shared artifacts: Deck - https://redwood.example/decks/cypherware-pathfinder; Benchmark spreadsheet (requested)

Auto-Gen Summary (brief, may be noisy):
Cypherware is evaluating open models and different hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC). Primary concerns: context length for long scientific documents, multilingual support for internal teams, function/tool-calling with internal knowledge connectors, and security/compliance (KMS, audit logs, SSO). They want a benchmark on their data and pricing for dedicated pilot.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Sofia's our solutions engineer. How's every— good?
[00:06] Anika: Yeah thanks, hi. Appreciate you folks coming on. We've got a short agenda— model pick, context length, tool-calling with our knowledge base, and deployment constraints.
[00:14] Jordan: Perfect. I'll run quick commercial framing then pass to Sofia for the deep technical.
[00:18] Priya: Quick note, timeline's tight — pilot target by mid-May ideally.
[00:23] Sofia: Great. So high-level Cypherware, correct me if I'm wrong, you're doing applied research workflows, lots of long-form doc ingestion, multi-lingual internal notes across EN/DE/JA, and a need to call internal tools (search, ticketing) from the model. Is that accurate?
[00:36] Anika: Yes, and also summarization over multi-doc chains — often 20–40k tokens of context across citations, tables, etc. We also have production SLAs for response time within 800ms p50 ideally for interactive features.
[00:50] Marcus: On infra we run in GCP primarily, and for compliance we need KMS, audit logs, and SSO — SAML. On-prem is a maybe but VPC/private deployment is preferred.
[01:02] Sofia: Good. So three areas we want to cover: model selection (open models vs smaller hosted variants), how Redwood handles long context and KV cache/prefix caching, and then deployment mode tradeoffs — Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, or Private VPC.
[01:15] Jordan: Also will quickly address pricing patterns so you can map cost to request patterns.

[01:20] Sofia: Starting with models — we see customers in research use-case gravitate to longer-context models: 32k and 128k variants. Options you probably asked about include recent open families like LLaMA-family forks, Mistral's long-context branches (where available), and specialist long-context models. There are also quantized variants we can run on Dedicated or Private to reduce cost.
[01:41] Anika: Specific names — we tested a few internally, but what's your recommendation for multilingual fidelity? We care about DE and JA especially.
[01:49] Sofia: For multilingual, model family matters. Some open models have stronger European language coverage; others are more English-optimized. For DE/JA, we've seen that certain Llama-derivatives with instruction-tuning do okay, but Mistral/Multi models often better. We usually recommend A/B testing at the prompt eval level — run your sample prompts across 3 candidate models and measure semantic similarity/fidelity and hallucination rates.
[02:13] Marcus: How does Redwood make that easy? We're not wanting to spin up 20 clusters.
[02:18] Sofia: Redwood Console supports per-route model pinning and quick rollouts; our evaluation toolkit can run batch prompts and return metrics — latency, tokens, perplexity proxies, hallucination flags. For heavier tests we can spin a Dedicated node pool with short-lived instances to emulate production throughput.
[02:34] Priya: You mentioned 128k context — what does that look like for cost and latency?
[02:39] Sofia: Longer contexts increase memory and kernel pressure. For 128k it's worth using models compiled for long sequence attention (ALiBi, sliding window, or sparse attention) plus quantization. On Redwood Hosted, we have limited long-context variants; Dedicated or Private is better for consistent 128k support and the associated GPU memory. Latency will be higher — expect 2–3x per-token time compared to 8k context, but batching and prefix/KV caching reduce amortized cost if you have repeated context.
[03:07] Anika: We do repeated context — same corpus references across many queries, so caching could help. How does your KV cache work?
[03:14] Sofia: We use an in-memory KV cache for autoregressive decode states. For prefix caching we do serialized request caching — so repeated prefixes can be served near instantly. There's some nuance with quantized runs and cache validity across model variants. We'll provide a note on cache lifetimes and invalidation strategies.
[03:30] Jordan: Quick commercial: Hosted API is fastest to iterate, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full control for compliance but has longer setup. Pricing: Hosted is per-token, Dedicated is committed monthly with options for burst. We'll send numbers.
[03:46] Marcus: For our security folks, will Redwood integrate with GCP KMS/HSM and SSO? And preserve audit logs for 13+ months?
[03:54] Sofia: Yes, VPC + Private deployments can integrate with customer KMS/HSM and SAML/SSO. Hosted has enterprise connectors for KMS and SSO but keys are often customer-managed via BYOK patterns. Audit retention is configurable with add-on retention tiers — we'll include the SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[04:13] Anika: How deterministic is function/tool-calling? We plan to call our internal search API and a citation resolver. We need reliable JSON outputs and strong safety about not leaking queries.
[04:23] Sofia: Redwood supports structured tool-calling patterns and function calling; we have a router that can enforce post-processing and schema validation. We also provide observability with example traces to show model outputs vs tool call payloads. For security we can redact PII and route calls inside your VPC so payloads never leave your network in Private deployments. In Hosted there are options to obfuscate or encrypt payloads.
[04:46] Priya: Any gotchas with routing to fallback models? We want a cheap fallback for non-critical queries.
[04:51] Sofia: You can set routing policies by cost/latency tier. For non-critical you can route to a smaller, quantized model. The only caveat is output consistency — fallback model outputs may differ, so we recommend sanity checks and automatic fallbacks for non-critical flows only.
[05:07] Jordan: Question for Cypherware: what's your expected qps and typical payload sizes?
[05:11] Anika: For interactive features maybe 20–40 RPS in peak, with avg prompt size around 2–4k tokens but some sessions glue multiple docs reaching 25–40k. Batch pipelines maybe 200 reqs/hour for indexing tasks.
[05:25] Marcus: Also latency SLOs — interactive 800ms p50, 1500ms p95. Is that realistic on Dedicated + quantization?
[05:33] Sofia: It's reasonable at p50 with aggressive batching and optimized kernels. P95 depends on tail queuing and whether the request needs a full 128k decode — that will push to seconds. We can mitigate with prefix caching and routing to smaller context replicas for quick responses.
[05:50] Anika: On multilingual evaluation, can you help run per-language tests? We'll need native speakers to validate outputs — that's on us but we'd like Redwood to provide automated flags for hallucinations and a scoring baseline.
[06:02] Sofia: Yes, our eval harness supports multi-language metrics and you can upload ground-truth or use proxy metrics. We'll pair you with a solutions rep to set thresholds.
[06:12] Jordan: Switching to procurement — what's typical contract length for Dedicated pilots?
[06:16] Jordan: (continues) Usually 3 months reserved capacity pilot with optional conversion to annual commit. We'll propose a pilot SOW.
[06:22] Priya: For billing separation across teams, do you support per-route billing or cost centers?
[06:27] Sofia: Console shows token-level cost and can break down by API key, route, or model. You can export to billing connectors.
[06:35] Marcus: On the Private deployment path — if we go on-prem later, how portable are model artifacts? Do we need to re-quantize?
[06:42] Sofia: We aim for model portability; the same model family can be deployed across Hosted/Dedicated/Private but compilation and quantization artifacts differ per hardware. We'll provide quantization recipes and test artifacts. Transitioning to on-prem typically requires re-compilation for your GPU stack and validation.
[06:57] Anika: Are there any limitations with tool-calling in Hosted? We have sensitive search indices.
[07:02] Sofia: Hosted can do encrypted payloads and function-calling patterns, but if you need zero-eavesdrop — VPC/Private keeps traffic internal. Some customers use Hosted for non-sensitive features and Private for sensitive routes.
[07:14] (brief cross-talk)
[07:18] Jordan: Let's talk pilot success criteria — Anika, what would your team consider a green outcome?
[07:23] Anika: 1) Model achieves at least 85% fidelity on our summarization eval across DE/JA/EN; 2) Interactive SLOs met p50/p95 as discussed for key flows; 3) Secure tool-calling with validated JSON schema and logs; 4) Cost estimate under X (we'll provide numbers).
[07:41] Sofia: Good, we'll map those to testcases and metrics. We'll propose two candidate models: a 32k-context multilingual open model and a 128k long-context specialty for longer chains.
[07:53] Marcus: Can you also show us how trace logs look? Our auditors want clear evidence for data flows.
[07:58] Sofia: Yes, we'll include sample audit logs and trace screenshots in the security pack.
[08:04] Priya: Scheduling — can we get the benchmark run next week?
[08:07] Jordan: We'll try to start the bench on Monday if we have your prompt set and a small sample of documents.
[08:12] Anika: We'll aim to send that by Friday.
[08:15] (audio blip)
[08:18] Sofia: One more technical nuance — if you use caching and routing across variants, you need to be careful about cache keys when models differ. We'll write up recommended cache key strategies.
[08:29] Marcus: Noted. Also, are there limits on concurrent KV cache size per customer?
[08:33] Sofia: On Hosted there are soft limits; on Dedicated/Private you can configure higher cache memory per node. We'll provide config examples.
[08:43] Anika: About hallucination rates — do you do model fine-tuning or RLAIF with Redwood?
[08:49] Sofia: Redwood itself doesn't fine-tune models in-host as a managed service for most customers but we support model version pinning and can help orchestrate fine-tune jobs with partner workflows or unmanaged customer-managed fine-tuning, then deploy the artifact. For RLHF/RLAIF approaches you might run experiments off-platform and bring the model in.
[09:04] Jordan: Okay we'll wrap with recap and next steps.
[09:08] Jordan: Recap — Jordan will send security pack and pilot pricing; Sofia will set up the benchmark harness and request sample data access; Anika will share prompts and expected context sizes; we'll schedule VPC/KMS deep dive. Any objections?
[09:22] Priya: Sounds good.
[09:24] Marcus: All good.
[09:26] Anika: Thanks all.
[09:29] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[09:32] (meeting ends)

Post-call notes (auto-gen, noisy):
- Customer leans toward Dedicated for predictable latency but wants Hosted as fallback.
- Key risks: 128k support and p95 latency; need for native-language fidelity.
- Action: run comparative eval of two models (32k multilingual + 128k long-context) and present results.

End transcript.
